claims.text: The founding proposal for Project BLUEBIRD went to him as Director of Central Intelligence. The memorandum of 5 April 1950 from the Chief of the CIA's Inspection and Security Staff is addressed to the Director of Central Intelligence and says on its face: 'In view of the extreme sensitivity of this project and its covert nature, it is deemed advisable to submit this project directly to you, rather than through the channel of the Projects Review Committee. Knowledge of this project should be restricted to the absolute minimum number of persons.' It asks him for approval and for an allocation of $65,515.

claims.text: The Director on that date was Hillenkoetter. The memorandum itself names only the office; the National Security Archive's catalogue record for it names him as the recipient, and this node already dates his tenure as DCI from May 1947 to October 1950 on a CIA-held clipping. The identification is Tier 2 because the document does not make it.

claims.text: The same document records that Hillenkoetter 'headed the Central Intelligence Agency from May 1947 to October 1950' and that he 'wants a Congressional investigation of the UFOs'. On the wartime and immediate post-war years he is quoted: 'I know that neither Russia nor this country had anything even approaching such high speeds and maneuvers.'

claims.source: CIA-RDP68-00046R000200090028-9, Enquirer, 4 March 1960, editorial 'Flying Saucers Again'; declassified in part 2014-06-12
claims.text: An Enquirer editorial of 4 March 1960, also held in CIA records, states that 'Admiral Hillenkoetter, former director of the Central Intelligence Agency, is a board member of the privately financed NICAP ... As such he has referred his conclusions to the Senate Space Committee, requesting an investigation.'

The same editorial records its own disagreement with him: 'WE CANNOT wholly agree with the respected Vice Adm. R. H. Hillenkoetter (ret.) that the Air Force is deceiving the public' -- which preserves his position as well as the paper's.

label: Roscoe H. Hillenkoetter
narrative:
The first Director of Central Intelligence went on the public record in 1960 saying that the objects were 'operating under intelligent control' and asking Congress to investigate, and the documents that establish it are held by the Central Intelligence Agency itself. A Worcester Gazette clipping of 1 June 1960, filed in CIA records and released in 2014, reports him declaring: 'The unknown objects are operating under intelligent control. It is imperative that we learn where the UFO's (unidentified flying objects) come from and what their purpose is.' The same clipping gives his tenure as DCI, May 1947 to October 1950, and reports that he wanted a congressional investigation. A second CIA-held clipping, an Enquirer editorial of 4 March 1960, independently records him as a board member of NICAP who 'has referred his conclusions to the Senate Space Committee, requesting an investigation' -- while itself disagreeing with him.

None of that requires MJ-12, and this board does not route him through it. The purported 1948 Hillenkoetter-to-Truman memo shown to be an emulation of a Marshall-to-Roosevelt letter is a claim about a document, not about the man, and nothing above depends on it. A negative finding points the same way as the Corso file: the National Security Archive's mirror of the FBI files on Hillenkoetter contains, across the sections searched, zero occurrences of NICAP, flying saucer, unidentified flying, Keyhoe, or the year 1960. His FBI file is not a UFO file.

The structural point is the ordering. A former DCI publicly contradicting the Air Force's public position, while sitting on the board of the organisation pressing for hearings, is a fact about the disclosure apparatus that the board should reach directly rather than through somebody else's narrative about a forgery.
